explanation: Analog computers accept and process continuously varying physical quantities (such as voltage, pressure, temperature, or mechanical rotation) represented as continuous wave signals.

option_feedback.reason: Digital computers process discrete binary digits (0 and 1) rather than continuous analog signals.
Hybrid computers combine both analog and digital processing rather than using only continuous signals.
Personal computers are general-purpose digital microcomputers that operate on discrete binary data.

explanation: Read Only Memory (ROM) is non-volatile primary memory that permanently retains its stored firmware/boot instructions without changing or losing data when power is turned off.

ROM is a type of primary (main) memory on the motherboard, not secondary storage like an HDD or SSD.

Neither Statement II nor Statement III accurately characterises a classic serial port.

current_mapping.description: explain the following types of system software: a. operating system, b. device drivers, c. utility programs, d. language processors;

stem: A type of an operating system that is designed to process data and generate responses to external events within a specified time frame is
explanation: Official AKU-EB 2025 Answer Key marks C (time sharing system) as the keyed option among the cuatro choices provided (where CPU time is sliced into rapid time-quanta to respond within a specified time frame, as real-time OS was not listed among the four options).

option_feedback.reason: A single-user system only specifies that one user can log in at a time, without guaranteeing rapid time-sliced response.

answer_review_note: Official key: C (time sharing system). current_mapping.description: explain the following types of system software: a. operating system, b. device drivers, c. utility programs, d. language processors;

A multi-user operating system allows multiple users to log in and access the computer at the same time.

explanation: Industrial safety systems like oil refinery temperature monitors require immediate, deterministic processing of sensor alerts without delay, which is the defining role of a Real-Time Operating System (RTOS).

current_mapping.description: differentiate between the synchronous and asynchronous data transmission methods;

stem: A transmission in which a data is transmitted through block by block method is known as
explanation: In synchronous data transmission, characters are grouped and transmitted continuously in large frames or blocks synchronised by a shared clock signal, without start/stop bits between individual bytes.

option_feedback.reason: Satellite transmission is an unguided wireless communication medium, not a framing/timing transmission method.
Microwave transmission is a line-of-sight wireless medium, not the block-by-block timing method.
Asynchronous transmission sends data character-by-character (one byte at a time) framed by start and stop bits.

current_mapping.description: describe data communication and its components, i.e., sender, message, medium, protocol and receiver;

stem: A physical pathway that is used to deliver the message between sender and receiver is
explanation: In a data communication system, the **transmission medium** (or communication channel) is the physical pathway (such as twisted-pair cable, fibre optic cable, or radio waves) over which the message travels from sender to receiver.

option_feedback.reason: A set of rules that governs data communication is called a protocol, not a physical pathway.
The message is the actual data or information being communicated, not the pathway.
Bandwidth is the data-carrying capacity of a channel, not the physical pathway itself.

current_mapping.description: describe data communication and its components, i.e., sender, message, medium, protocol and receiver;

explanation: A communication **protocol** defines the rules, syntax, semantics, and timing that ensure exchanged data is properly formatted and mutually understood between sender and receiver.

option_feedback.reason: The sender is the device that originates the message.
The receiver is the destination device that accepts the message.
The transmission medium is the physical path carrying the raw signal, not the formatting rules.

current_mapping.description: describe data communication and its components, i.e., sender, message, medium, protocol and receiver;

stem: All of the following are the characteristics of a good communication system EXCEPT
explanation: The fundamental effectiveness characteristics of a good data communication system are **delivery**, **accuracy**, **timeliness**, and **jitter**; a **protocol** is one of the five *components* of a communication system, not a performance characteristic.

option_feedback.reason: Delivery (delivering data to the correct destination) is a core characteristic of a good communication system.
Accuracy (delivering data without unaltered/corrupted bits) is a core characteristic of a good communication system.
Timeliness (delivering data in a timely manner without significant delay) is a core characteristic of a good communication system.

current_mapping.description: distinguish among the memory measuring units such as bits, bytes, kilobytes, megabytes, and gigabytes in computer memory;

stem: On converting 3 Mib (Mebibyte) into Kibibyte, the value will be
explanation: Since $1\text{ MiB (Mebibyte)} = 2^{10}\text{ KiB} = 1024\text{ KiB (Kibibytes)}$, converting $3\text{ MiB}$ gives $3 \times 1024 = 3072\text{ KiB}$.

option_feedback.reason: 3000 uses the decimal factor 1000 instead of the binary factor $1024$ ($2^{10}$) required for Mebibytes to Kibibytes.
3000000 multiplies by $10^6$ (bytes in decimal MB), not Kibibytes.
$3145728 = 3 \times 1024 \times 1024$ converts $3\text{ MiB}$ into **bytes**, not Kibibytes.

stem: If the bit rate of the signal is 2000 bps and each signal unit carries 2 bits, then the baud rate of the signal will be
explanation: Baud rate is given by $\text{Baud Rate} = \frac{\text{Bit Rate}}{\text{Bits per signal unit}} = \frac{2000\text{ bps}}{2\text{ bits/baud}} = 1000\text{ baud}$.

option_feedback.reason: 100 divides 2000 by 20 instead of 2.
1020 is an unrelated arithmetic distractor.
4000 multiplies $2000 \times 2$ instead of dividing bit rate by the number of bits per signal element.

stem: If the strength of a signal falls off when the distance increases, then the type of transmission impairment will be
explanation: **Attenuation** is the gradual loss or weakening of signal strength (amplitude) as it travels over increasing distance through a transmission medium.

option_feedback.reason: Crosstalk is unwanted electromagnetic interference induced from one adjacent wire/channel into another.
Distortion occurs when different frequency components of a composite signal travel at different speeds and alter the signal shape.
Amplification is the boosting of signal strength using an amplifier/repeater to overcome attenuation, not an impairment.

explanation: In a **client/server network architecture**, multiple client workstations (employees) connect to a dedicated central server that manages shared resources, files, authentication, and services.

option_feedback.reason: A Wide Area Network (WAN) classifies a network by geographical span rather than central server vs peer architecture.
In a peer-to-peer (P2P) network, all nodes have equal status and share resources directly without a central server.
A point-to-point network links only two endpoints directly rather than connecting multiple employees to a central server.

stem:

• Easy to detect errors
• Easy to add or remove nodes

Based on the given properties, the network topology is identified as
explanation: In a **star topology**, every computer node connects directly to a central hub or switch, making it easy to isolate faults and add or remove individual nodes without disrupting the rest of the network.

option_feedback.reason: Bus topology connects all nodes along a single linear backbone cable without a central hub.
Ring topology connects nodes in a closed circular loop without a central hub.
Mesh topology connects every node directly to every other node rather than relying on a central hub.

explanation: Both commercial radio broadcasting (station to listener) and standard computer-to-printer data transmission flow in one direction only (unidirectional), which defines **simplex transmission**.

current_mapping.description: explain computer networks and their uses in different fields;

II. It allows sharing of the internet.

explanation: Computer networks allow multiple users to share application software over a network (I) and share a single internet connection (II). Statements III and IV are false because networks can transfer large files and always require wired or wireless transmission media.

option_feedback.reason: Statement III is false because computer networks can transfer both small and very large files.
Statement IV is false because every computer network requires either guided (wired) or unguided (wireless) transmission media.

explanation: A network connecting employees within a single building, office, or campus is a **Local Area Network (LAN)**.

option_feedback.reason: A WAN spans across countries, continents, or the entire globe, not a single company campus.
A PAN covers only a few metres around a single individual's personal devices (e.g., Bluetooth headset).
A MAN spans an entire city or metropolitan area rather than a single company campus.

current_mapping.description: describe the modes of network communication, i.e., simplex, half duplex and full duplex;

stem: Watching a movie on television and text messaging on a mobile phone are the examples of
explanation: Watching television is unidirectional (**simplex**), while sending and receiving SMS text messages back and forth one message at a time is bidirectional but one turn at a time (**half-duplex**).

option_feedback.reason: Television broadcasting is one-way (simplex), not two-way simultaneous (full-duplex).

Turn-based SMS text messaging is classified as half-duplex rather than simultaneous full-duplex voice calling.

A MAN is limited to a single city or town rather than connecting devices across the world.
